correctness.rationale: The proof derives the all-assignment cut criterion via integral edge-orientation flow, then bounds VC by degree-three cuts and exhibits the K4 disjoint K3 witness. In independent V8 verification of the actual package depth11_tree.json (Git blob 4339ed5a45be4e1d869520bae2db99ee587c9483), all 2047 internal queries and 2048 distinct leaf masks were checked against their entire eleven-bit paths; all leaf tournaments had outdegree three. Separately enumerating all 2^21 edge orientations gave 2640 regular tournaments, excluding depth 12 since 2640<4096. Independently compiled C++ evaluated all 2,097,152 seven-vertex edge supports against every cut and returned coefficients (1,21,210,1330,5880,18732,40502,32490,315,35), zero thereafter. The claimed small orders follow from 2 and 24 hypotheses and K2+K1/K3+K2 supports.
residual_risks: Finite exhaustive verification is restricted to its specified domain.

value.rationale: This determines the first failure of equality between fixed and adaptive shattering dimensions for a natural score-constrained orientation class. The sharp 11-round certificate and entire intermediate static support census give precise query-learning benchmarks not mechanically implied by the earlier all-order static VC extremal theorem.
residual_risks: The value is finite or parameter-specific and should not be promoted as an all-parameter theorem.

final_claim: Regular tournament edge-orientation classes first have VC/Littlestone gap at seven vertices: VC=9 and Littlestone=11; exact seven-vertex shattered-support polynomial and 35 K4+K3 extremizers.
limitations: No general Littlestone formula at all odd orders, nor unbounded separation.
